<p class="eyebrow">Associate Professor of Economics · Carleton University</p>

# Matthew D. Webb

<p class="research-line">Applied Microeconometrics <span>·</span> Causal Inference <span>·</span> Machine Learning and AI for Economic Measurement <span>·</span> Empirical Microeconomics</p>

I develop and apply econometric methods for credible empirical research, with a particular focus on inference with clustered data and difference-in-differences designs. My current work also uses machine learning and AI to measure economically meaningful features in images and other complex data.

## Current Research

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Using Images as Covariates

Measuring curb appeal with deep learning and integrating image-derived information into economic models.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19915) · [Research overview](research.qmd#ai-machine-learning-and-economic-measurement)
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Improved Inference for CSDID

Cluster-jackknife inference for modern difference-in-differences estimators.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12043) · [Watch video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8xLv7Bu-_l0)
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### DID-INT and UN-DID

Methods for difference-in-differences with covariate-effect heterogeneity and with data that cannot be pooled.

[DID-INT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14447) · [UN-DID](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.15910)
:::
:::

## Research Software

The [Software page](software.qmd) is a curated guide to implementations of my research methods across Stata, R, Julia, and Python. It groups software by method, gives verified installation commands, connects each implementation to its paper, and credits the implementation author.
